headline: Broad-based growth with wider margins and a new buyback
summary_short: Revenue was $2,169.2M, up 23.5% y/y, with gross margin at 59.3% and Adjusted EBITDA of $465.3M (21.5% margin). Direct-to-consumer revenue grew 36.0%.
summary_long: Revenue rose across all three segments, led by volume growth in Technical Apparel and Outdoor Performance. Greater China grew 30.4% and the Americas 22.2%. Gross margin expanded on mix and lower tariff costs. SG&A grew 21.9% on store expansion and personnel. Cash was $668.1M. The board authorized a $1.0B share repurchase on November 12; none had been bought yet. 2026 capex is expected near $400M.
confidence_notes: IFRS basis (6-K MD&A, Exhibit 99.1). Shard EPS ($0.42) is Yahoo data; its y/y prior ($0.03) does not reconcile with reported net income of $239.6M vs $143.1M, so only the q/q delta is shown. The release states no next-quarter guidance.

drivers.explanation: Revenue increased across all segments, primarily on volume growth in Technical Apparel and Outdoor Performance. DTC rose 36.0%, and Greater China and the Americas led regional growth.
Gains came from favorable channel, segment, region, product and pricing mix plus lower tariff costs, partly offset by higher transportation costs.
SG&A grew 21.9%, mainly on higher personnel, advertising and rent, tied to DTC store expansion and investment in Greater China and Asia Pacific.
